name: Touriga Franca

lines.s10: Touriga Franca is the Douro's dependable red, juicy and perfumed: blackberry, black plum and rose petal, softer than Touriga Nacional.
lines.s20: Touriga Franca grows across the Douro and gives Port and the dry reds their flesh and perfume. It is lighter and juicier than Touriga Nacional, with blackberry, rose petal and a firm but supple grip.
lines.s45: Touriga Franca seldom works alone: it is the other half of many Douro blends. It is at home on the Douro's hot schist, ripening late and cropping reliably. In the glass it is deep red, with blackberry, black plum and rose petal. It is lighter and juicier than Touriga Nacional, with fresh acidity and a firm but supple grip. The two are blended for Port and dry Douro reds: Nacional gives structure, and Franca flesh and perfume. Pour it with grilled lamb, roast pork or cured ham. DNA shows it is a child of Touriga Nacional, so in many a Douro blend parent and child share the glass.
lines.sale: Touriga Franca is the softer, more fragrant side of the Douro: blackberry and rose petal with a grip that stays gentle. It suits the roast pork, and any table that finds Touriga Nacional too much.

glass.lead: Blackberry, black plum and rose petal in a deep red glass, juicy and medium plus in body, with fresh acidity and a supple grip.

ladder.where: The higher, cooler slopes of the Douro
The Cima Corgo and the Douro Superior

glass.structure: Dry. Acidity medium plus, tannin medium plus to high, firm but velvety, alcohol medium plus, body medium plus.

home.home: The Douro, where it ripens late and crops reliably on the hot schist slopes. It is blended with Touriga Nacional and the other favoured grapes for Port and for the dry Douro reds, bringing flesh and a rose petal perfume, and a few cellars bottle it alone.
home.abroad: It seldom leaves northern Portugal. California grows a little, in Lodi and elsewhere, where a bottle labelled simply Touriga is often this grape.

service.temp: 61 to 64 degrees Fahrenheit, 16 to 18 degrees Celsius, as for a full red or a Vintage Port.
service.glass: A tall Bordeaux glass for the dry wines; a small tulip for Port.
service.decant: Consider it for a young dry red after tasting a sample; decant a Vintage Port off its crust.
service.age: Most dry reds within five to ten years; within a Vintage Port blend, for decades.

with.why: juicy fruit and a supple grip suit the char
fresh acidity and gentle tannin cut the fat
rose petal and dark fruit beside rich, salty duck

labels.means: The older name of Touriga Franca, still seen on some labels; the grape has no French origin.
Dry reds of the Port valley, often blends of Touriga Franca and Touriga Nacional.
Fortified red from the Douro; Touriga Franca is one of its five favoured grapes.

guest.q: Is Touriga Franca related to Touriga Nacional?
guest.a: Yes, it is its child: DNA shows a cross of Touriga Nacional and an old Douro grape called Marufo. It is lighter and juicier than its parent, with more rose petal in the perfume.
No. Its old name, Touriga Francesa, sounds French, but it is a Portuguese grape of the Douro, and Portugal now calls it Touriga Franca.

guest.q: Why is it so often blended?
guest.a: On its own it is supple and perfumed but a little less deep than Touriga Nacional. Together they balance: Nacional gives the structure, Franca the flesh and fragrance.

compare.tell: Touriga Nacional, its parent, is darker and firmer, with violet and bergamot; Touriga Franca is lighter and juicier, with rose petal and a suppler grip.
Tinta Roriz, Tempranillo in the Douro, is rounder and softer in acidity, with strawberry and red plum; Touriga Franca is more perfumed, with rose petal and a firmer grip.

profile.st: Deep ruby to purple · Body medium plus · Acid medium plus · Tannin medium plus to high, firm but velvety · Alcohol medium plus · Dry
profile.fruit: Blackberry, black cherry and black plum, with a tang of pomegranate
profile.other: Rose petal and rockrose; vanilla and toast where French oak is used; a supple, juicy texture
profile.tell: Blackberry and rose petal with a supple grip: the softer, more fragrant partner beside Touriga Nacional in a Douro blend
profile.regions: The Douro, for Port and dry reds; a little elsewhere in northern Portugal and in California
profile.confuse: Touriga Nacional is darker and firmer, with violet and bergamot; Tinta Roriz is rounder and softer in acidity, with strawberry and red plum

cards.front: Touriga Franca: who are its parents, and what was its old name?
cards.back: Touriga Nacional and Marufo, by DNA. Its old name was Touriga Francesa, though the grape has no French origin.

cards.front: What does Touriga Franca bring to a Port or Douro blend?
cards.back: Flesh, juicy blackberry and a perfume of rose petal and rockrose, beside the depth and structure of Touriga Nacional.

cards.front: Why do Douro growers value Touriga Franca on hot sites?
cards.back: It ripens late and crops reliably in the heat, and its thick skins give colour and tannin.

questions.q: A guest sees Touriga Francesa on an older Port list and asks whether it is a French grape. What do you tell him?
opts: No: it is Touriga Franca, a Portuguese grape
Yes: it came from Bordeaux in the 1800s
No: it is an old name for Tempranillo
Yes: it is Portugal's name for Cabernet Franc
questions.exp: Touriga Francesa is the older name of Touriga Franca, a Portuguese grape born of Touriga Nacional and Marufo. Cabernet Franc, the nearest miss in sound, is no relation.

questions.q: A dry Douro red poured blind is deep red but supple, with blackberry, black cherry and rose petal, fresh acidity and a gentler grip than a Touriga Nacional. Which grape leads it?
questions.exp: Blackberry with rose petal and a supple grip mark Touriga Franca. Tinta Barroca, the nearest miss, is soft and fleshy too, but it ripens early, is planted on cooler sites and is prized for sugar.

questions.q: A guest asks why a Douro red blends Touriga Franca with Touriga Nacional instead of bottling either alone. What is the usual reason?
opts: Nacional gives structure, Franca flesh and perfume
The law forbids a single grape Douro red
Franca adds sweetness to the dry wine
Nacional cannot ripen on the schist
questions.exp: Touriga Nacional brings depth and firm tannin, Touriga Franca juicy fruit and a rose petal perfume, so each fills out the other. Douro law allows a varietal red, so the law is the nearest wrong answer.

report: A new grape, mode home as the plan fixes it. No TASTE row exists, so nothing can contradict TASTE.world.

Late ripening and reliable on hot sites, floral and juicy, the flesh and perfume of the blend, one of the five favoured Port grapes, French oak for the dry reds and the Douro's sub-regions stand on the Codex's own Douro record. The glass stands on Wines of Portugal (deep colour, blackberry, rose and rockrose, firm but velvety tannin) and Wine Folly (blackberry, rose petal, pomegranate), with trade pages agreeing that it is lighter and more perfumed than Touriga Nacional.

Parentage, Touriga Nacional and Marufo, stands on the Wein-Plus glossary and Wine Grapes, with a 2011 DNA analysis in the journal VITIS seen through search. The renaming from Touriga Francesa is given without its year, which only one source gave as 2000.
California, Lodi above all, stands on two trade pages seen through search; no other country is named for want of sources. Thick skins giving colour and tannin stand on two trade pages.

The Codex's Douro record calls Touriga Franca the most planted grape of the Douro and its question r-rlbnb9nk asks for the most widely planted grape; both are volatile rankings the house rules keep out of new prose, and that question will join this grape's drill.
